title: Best Power Banks UK
short: Portable chargers compared by capacity, output speed and weight, from pocket-sized to laptop-charging capacity.
intro: A power bank's capacity and output wattage both matter: capacity determines how many charges you get, while wattage determines how fast. This guide compares power banks tested by Expert Reviews, from ultra-portable budget picks to laptop-charging capacity units.

products.name: Prime A110A
products.best_for: Buyers who want maximum capacity and charging speed in one unit
products.summary: Expert Reviews praises the outstanding charging speeds and useful digital display, with touchscreen monitoring and Bluetooth app connectivity, though it's expensive and bulky at 600g.

products.name: 10 Mini
products.best_for: Buyers who want an affordable, pocketable everyday charger
products.summary: Highly portable with an LED display and excellent value, though it has no wireless charging and its peak speeds are limited to specific devices.
cons: Peak speeds limited to specific devices

guide.q: What capacity power bank do I need?
guide.a: As a rough guide, 10,000mAh gives most phones 2-3 full charges in a pocketable size. 20,000mAh-plus suits longer trips, multiple devices, or charging a tablet. Laptop charging generally needs at least 20,000mAh (around 74Wh or more) and a high-wattage USB-C output.

guide.q: Can I take a power bank on a plane?
guide.a: Airlines generally require power banks to be carried in hand luggage, not the hold, and most cap capacity at 100Wh (roughly 27,000mAh) without special permission. Always check your specific airline's rules before flying, as they can vary.

guide.q: Does wattage matter as much as capacity?
guide.a: Yes. A higher-capacity bank with low wattage output will charge your phone slowly. Match the output wattage to what your device can actually accept for fast charging, since exceeding your phone's own charging limit provides no extra speed.

guide.q: Is wireless charging worth having on a power bank?
guide.a: Wireless charging is convenient, particularly with MagSafe-style magnetic attachment, but it's generally slower and less efficient than a cable. It's a nice-to-have rather than essential if you always have a cable to hand.
